description: How computer science research is planned, done, evaluated and communicated, from a question to a defended proposal and a final-year project that can withstand review. Taught to the depth of a graduate research methods seminar, with every stage practised on the student's own project.
modelledOn: Dawson, Projects in Computing and Information Systems: A Student's Guide
Creswell and Creswell, Research Design: Qualitative, Quantitative and Mixed Methods Approaches
ACM Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct
outcomes: Distinguish scientific knowledge from opinion and classify research by purpose, method and contribution.
Find, read, critique and synthesise the literature on a topic and write a structured literature review.
Formulate research questions and hypotheses and choose an appropriate research design.
Plan a project with scope, milestones, risks and ethical approval.
Collect and analyse quantitative and qualitative data with the correct statistics and reporting.
Write a research proposal and project report and present and defend the work.

units.title: Overview of research and scientific knowledge
topics: What research is: systematic inquiry, reproducibility, falsifiability; science versus engineering versus design
Kinds of knowledge and sources of truth; the scientific method and its limits
Research in computer science: theory, experiments, systems building, empirical software engineering, human studies
Contributions: new algorithms, tools, evidence, taxonomies; what counts as novelty
Reading a research paper: structure, claims, evidence, limitations

units.title: Research as communication
topics: Venues: journals, conferences, workshops, preprints; peer review and impact
Scientific writing: clarity, precision, structure, citing; avoiding plagiarism
Reference management (Zotero, BibTeX) and citation styles (ACM, IEEE, APA)
Presenting: talks, posters, demonstrations; writing for non-experts and funders

units.title: Ethics
topics: Research integrity: fabrication, falsification, plagiarism, authorship, conflicts of interest
Human participants: informed consent, anonymity, data protection (Ghana's Data Protection Act), vulnerable groups
Ethics review boards and institutional approval; ethics in AI, security and data research
Responsible use of generative AI in research and writing

units.title: Types of research projects
topics: Basic and applied; exploratory, descriptive, explanatory, evaluative
Quantitative, qualitative and mixed methods; experiments, surveys, case studies, action research, design science
Development projects versus research projects; the artefact plus evaluation model
Choosing a topic: feasibility, interest, supervisor fit, local relevance

units.title: Literature review and critique
topics: Searching: databases (ACM DL, IEEE Xplore, Google Scholar, arXiv), keywords, snowballing, inclusion criteria
Systematic literature reviews and mapping studies; keeping a search log
Critical appraisal: validity, sample, methods, bias, reproducibility
Synthesis: themes, gaps, tables of comparison; writing the review, not a list of summaries
Workshop: reviewing ten papers on the student's topic

units.title: Research and project planning
topics: From topic to research questions, aims, objectives and hypotheses; scope and boundaries
Work plans, Gantt charts, milestones, deliverables, supervision meetings
Risk assessment and contingency; resources, tools and data access
Time management and keeping a research diary

units.title: Research design and data collection
topics: Variables, operationalisation, validity (internal, external, construct) and reliability
Experimental design: controls, randomisation, between and within subjects, benchmarks for algorithm and system evaluation
Surveys and questionnaires; interviews and focus groups; observation; sampling strategies
Measurement in computing: performance metrics, usability metrics (SUS), accuracy metrics
Pilot studies and pre-registration

units.title: Data analysis
topics: Descriptive statistics and visualisation; choosing the right chart
Inferential statistics: t-tests, ANOVA, chi-square, correlation, regression, non-parametric tests; effect sizes and confidence intervals; p-value pitfalls
Qualitative analysis: coding, thematic analysis, grounded theory in brief
Tools: R, Python, SPSS, NVivo; reproducible analysis scripts
Threats to validity and how to report them honestly

units.title: Structure of a research proposal
topics: Title, abstract, introduction and motivation, problem statement, research questions, objectives
Literature review, methodology, expected outcomes, timeline, budget, references
Writing and peer-reviewing proposals in class; responding to feedback
Proposal defence

units.title: Structure of a research project report
topics: Chapters: introduction, literature review, methodology, design and implementation, results and evaluation, discussion, conclusion and future work
Appendices, code and data availability, reproducibility packages
Figures, tables and captions; abstracts and executive summaries
Final presentation and viva preparation; turning a project into a paper

schedule.title: What research is
schedule.exercise: Classify five published computing papers by their research type and say what each one contributes.

tasks.title: Judge six statements as science, engineering or design work and test which are falsifiable, from a scored scenario
Evaluate four claims of knowledge, such as a vendor benchmark or an expert opinion, against evidence quality in a scored case
Match five research projects to theory, experiment, system building, empirical software engineering or human studies, and justify each match

schedule.title: Contributions and reading papers
schedule.exercise: Read one paper and write half a page covering its problem, claim, evidence, limits and your verdict.

tasks.title: Identify the contribution type and novelty of three abstracts and rank them by how convincingly novelty is argued
Read a short paper case and extract its claims, the evidence for each and the stated limitations, scored against the rubric
Reproduce the main figure of a short paper from its published data in code and judge whether the claim holds

schedule.title: Venues, writing and referencing
schedule.exercise: Write a 150-word abstract for your own project, then a revised version for a non-expert audience.

tasks.title: Choose a venue for four finished studies by comparing peer review, impact and audience, and justify each choice
Rewrite five unclear sentences from a draft and detect three cases of copied text, scored against a clarity and plagiarism rubric
Convert a list of 12 references from one style to ACM, IEEE and APA using a script and a BibTeX file, and check for errors

schedule.title: Research integrity and ethics
schedule.exercise: Prepare the ethics application for a survey of students on phone use, including the consent form and data plan.

tasks.title: Spot the fabrication, falsification and authorship problems in a described project and recommend the report route
Design consent, anonymity and data storage for interviews with vulnerable farmers, and be scored on data protection compliance
Decide how generative AI may be used in a literature review and thesis, in a scored scenario with disclosure and verification choices

schedule.title: Research types and topics
schedule.exercise: Write a short paragraph choosing the research approach for a mobile money usability question, with reasons.

tasks.title: Classify six research questions as exploratory, descriptive, explanatory or evaluative, and choose a suitable approach for each
Choose among experiment, survey, case study, action research or design science for four problems and justify each
Compare three candidate topics for feasibility, interest, supervisor fit and local relevance in a scored scenario and pick one

schedule.title: Searching and appraising literature
schedule.exercise: Write a search strategy with keywords, databases, inclusion criteria and a log for your topic.

tasks.title: Build search strings for four research questions and choose inclusion criteria, scored against the number and relevance of papers returned
Record a search log of 60 papers in a table, screen by title and abstract, and compute the counts at each stage for a flow diagram
Appraise three studies for validity, sample, method and bias in a scored scenario and rank them by trustworthiness

schedule.title: Synthesising the literature
schedule.exercise: Draft the synthesis paragraph of a literature review that compares ten papers by theme, not one at a time.

tasks.title: Code ten papers into themes in a comparison table and count how many address each theme to show where the gaps are
Identify the gap, the competing findings and the weak evidence in a set of papers, and write a synthesis scored against the rubric
Review ten papers on a given topic, record appraisal ratings, and argue for one research gap supported by the evidence

schedule.title: Planning a research project
schedule.exercise: Write the aims, objectives and work plan of your project, with a Gantt chart and the top three risks.

tasks.title: Turn a broad topic into a research question, aims, objectives and a hypothesis, scored on being specific and testable
Order tasks, milestones and supervision meetings into a feasible plan for a 12-week project and fix the one critical-path delay
Assess the risks, data access and resource problems in a project and choose contingency plans that satisfy the rubric

schedule.title: Methods and measurement
schedule.exercise: Design the evaluation of a new mobile app, stating variables, metrics, sample and threats to validity.

tasks.title: Operationalise four abstract concepts into measurable variables and identify the validity and reliability threat of each
Design and simulate a randomised experiment comparing two sorting algorithms on 30 inputs each, with controls, and report the difference
Compute a SUS score for 15 respondents, compare it with the benchmark mean of 68, and report accuracy metrics for a classifier

schedule.title: Analysing data
schedule.exercise: Write the analysis plan for a survey of 100 students, stating which tests you will use and why.

tasks.title: Describe a survey dataset with summary statistics and choose the right chart for each of four variables
Choose and run the correct test for three questions (two groups, three groups, two categories), with effect sizes and confidence intervals
Code twelve interview excerpts into themes, merge overlapping codes, and be scored on whether the themes are supported by the data

schedule.title: Reproducible analysis and threats to validity
schedule.exercise: Write the threats-to-validity section for a small experiment and propose how you would limit each threat.

tasks.title: Write a script that loads a dataset, runs two tests and saves tables and figures, and verify a colleague can rerun it with identical output
Rate the threats to validity in a described study and write an honest limitations paragraph, scored on candour and specificity
Compare a study analysed with and without controlling for a confounder in code, then write the validity threats it still faces and how to report them

schedule.title: Writing and defending proposals
schedule.exercise: Peer-review a classmate's proposal with a rubric and prepare a five-minute defence with answers to three expected questions.

tasks.title: Write the title, abstract and research questions of a proposal for a given problem and be scored on clarity, scope and feasibility
Complete the methodology, timeline and budget of a given proposal skeleton and be scored on fit between method and research question
Review a flawed proposal with a rubric, write balanced feedback, and respond to a mock reviewer's three comments
Defend a proposal against a panel's questions on novelty, method and feasibility, choosing the best response in each exchange

schedule.title: Writing up and presenting
schedule.exercise: Outline the final report for your project, chapter by chapter, with one sentence on what each chapter must prove.

tasks.title: Assign eight paragraphs to the right chapters of a dissertation and fix the structure so each chapter does its job
Package a small analysis as a reproducibility bundle with data, code, a README and a run script, and verify it runs from a clean folder
Prepare and deliver a final presentation and viva, choose the slides to keep within 10 minutes, and answer five questions scored by rubric
